newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan airline expects $28.4 mln 1997 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan airline expects $28.4 mln 1997 net profit.

text.p: Morocco's Royal Air Maroc (RAM), on Tuesday said it expects net profit of 270 million dirhams ($28.4 million) by the end of 1997, up from 145 million dirhams in 1996.

"According to the positive indicators registered in the first quarter of the year, Royal Air Maroc expects a net profit of 270 million dirhams, up from 145 million dirhams in 1996," Mohamed Hassad, RAM chairman told a news conference held the firm's headquarters on Tuesday evening.
Hassad, who anounced the company's 1996 results said the airline turnover rose 1.5 percent to 4.7 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with 1995.
"Net profits nearly doubled to 145 million dirhams in 1996 from 78 million dirhams in 1995," Hassad told reporters.

Despite the tariffs drop by an average minus five percent and a rise of aircrafts' fuel by 25 percent in 1996, the firm reached "these good results thanks to the downsizing costs policy," Hassad added.
The airline also launched a 1997-2001 strategic plan aimed at modernising the firm's 27 aircraft fleet and reducing the debt ratio to 1.9 by the year 2001 from the current 2.4, Hassad said.
"Our prime target is to go beyond the 6.0 billion dirhams turnover in the coming years in order to realise an annual net profit of 5.0 percent of the total turnover," he said.
